name: Sir Noah Thorn
title: The Fallen Knight
nickname: The Fallen Knight; "the Knight of Ashford"

origin.birthplace: Thornhold, the border fortress in the east
origin.socialStatus: Stripped of title and lands, lives as a sellsword
origin.profession: Once a famous knight, commander of cavalry

appearance.face: A weathered face, straight nose, deep lines around the eyes; a notched ear
appearance.hairAndEyes: Short greying chestnut hair; thick beard; tired blue eyes
appearance.clothing: Worn armour without a crest (the crest has been scraped off); an old sword; a patched cloak
appearance.build: Broad-shouldered, a soldier's posture even when exhausted
appearance.gestures: Touches the scraped-off crest when thinking; never sits with his back to the door
appearance.voice: Low, firm voice; speaks briefly and plainly
appearance.firstImpression: A proud, grim man who looks like a knight even without a title
appearance.artistNotes: Where the crest was scraped off, a pale patch shows on the armour. He wears an old locket with his wife's name.

backstory.biography: Noah Thorn led the cavalry at the battle of Ashford. When the flank was surrounded he pulled his riders back to save his men, and the battle was lost. The court needed someone to blame and found him: accused of cowardice, stripped of title and lands. His wife died in poverty while he fought the verdict. Today he is a sellsword and caravan guard.
backstory.whyHere: He wants to win enough to buy back his title and restore the honour of his name.
backstory.secret: That he is no longer sure he did the right thing at Ashford. He saved his men but lost the battle, and the thought will not leave him.

psychology.weakness: His pride will not let him back down when insulted
psychology.fear: Dying a traitor without anyone knowing the truth
psychology.desire: To clear his name and his family's
psychology.angers: Lies, cowardice, insults to his honour
psychology.regret: His wife's death, the retreat at Ashford
psychology.moralLimits: Does not lie, does not steal, does not strike an unarmed man
psychology.wouldForReward: Risk his life — but not his honour

behavior.stakes: Prefers honest stakes. Can risk a lot if challenged
behavior.deception: Does not cheat. Accepts a bluff as part of the game, but not a lie
behavior.debts: Pays his debts at any cost
behavior.alliances: Extremely loyal if the ally is honest
behavior.whenAttacks: When insulted, or defending an ally
behavior.whenRetreats: When continuing would mean breaking his word
behavior.onLoss: Accepts defeat with dignity, but remembers a deception
behavior.strategyChange: When he finds an ally has lied to him

motives.publicGoal: To win enough to buy back his title
motives.hiddenGoal: To restore the honour of his name and his wife's
motives.personalReason: To prove an honest man can also win
motives.betrayalTrigger: Nothing — unless an ally turns out to be a liar
motives.helpTrigger: If someone is cheated or humiliated unfairly

speech.howLies: Barely lies. When he tries, it is obvious. He keeps silent rather than lie
speech.angerAndFear: Goes quiet and pale. Sits upright and touches his sword hilt

mechanics.strangeness: The locket with his wife's name grows warm when someone at the table lies. Noah does not know whether it is a gift or a curse.
mechanics.temptation: His pride will not let him back down when insulted
mechanics.ability: Oath: once per evening he swears his gift is honest — and the host confirms it to the table if it is true.
mechanics.hostRelation: Hatred — he sees in the host everything that destroyed his honour.

authorNotes.distinctive: A tragic, honest hero in a game full of cheats. The moral centre of the table.
authorNotes.immutable: The honour and the doubt about Ashford.
authorNotes.tunable: How easily he flares up at insults.

lines.text: Noah Thorn. No "sir". No lands. But I have my word.
I lost honestly. That is more than some can say.
Say that again — with a sword in your hand.
An alliance is a promise. Can I trust you?
So you are like them too.
If I stake, I stake everything.
Noah Thorn. Once "sir". They say he ran at Ashford — say it to his face, if you dare.
At the same table again. Good. I remember how you play.
Tell them… I did not run.

tells.description: Touches the scraped-off crest on his armour
Turns pale and touches his sword hilt
Looks away when he lies — he lies badly
